items.note: The page defines frames on sources, gates and sinks, the edge change $D_vD_u^{-1}$, $D_{\rm in}$, $D_{\rm out}$ and $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$, proves the invariant and reaches $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$. It then concludes that only endpoint frames matter and that interior frames can be chosen for cheap edges, as the paper does (lines 785-825).

The page inducts along the wires with the paper's three cases. At a source the invariant is the definition of $g$. On an edge, "$D_vD_u^{-1}D_u\varphi=D_v\varphi$". At a gate, the common frame on all incidences gives "$\sum_j c_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_j c_j\varphi_j)$". At the sinks this yields $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$.

The page writes "Then that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ ..., auxiliary roles included" as an immediate consequence of the displayed identity, the paper's own "In particular". It leaves implicit the reading-off of the $(\rho(w),w)$ block from the block-diagonal $D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, $D_{\rm out}$ and the signed permutation $\mathsf S_\Omega$. The separate "Interior frames cancel" telescoping paragraph does not supply that argument and is flagged under errors.

errors.quote: A route through a vertex $m$ from a source $s$ to a sink $t$ applies $D_mD_s^{-1}$ and then $D_tD_m^{-1}$, whose product is $D_tD_s^{-1}$ for every $D_m$.
errors.problem: This multiplies only the edge operators and leaves out the pointwise gate at $m$ that acts between them. $D_m^{-1}$ cancels against $D_m$ only because that gate commutes with its common frame (the paper's step $\sum_j c_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_j c_j\varphi_j)$). In a signed role permutation, the route from $\mathrm{source}(w)$ to $\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))$ also passes through gates that mix wires (for example $X_a$ ends on $Y_a$'s sink), so it is not a single wire path, and the telescoping produces no sign $\varepsilon_w$. The paper gets the route operator only from $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$ (lines 813-825). The page's earlier invariant already gives the correct reason, so the main argument still holds.
